answer: A hardware-bound stake bond stops fake agents. Each agent locks 1,000 POA behind a TPM chip fingerprint before trading, so one operator cannot spin up a thousand identities from one laptop. The bond unlocks only after 30 days of honest transactions; peers audit the ledger weekly, and detected fraud slashes the full 1,000 POA and burns the fingerprint. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake agents would need 1,000,000 POA plus 1,000 TPM chips, roughly $40,000 in hardware alone. Like a glacier grinding down a ridge, honest time wears fakes away while real agents wander freely across the market.
